children: Tata Group stocks will remain in focus amid a keen tussle among top stakeholders. Legal opinions obtained by Tata Sons support the validity of N Chandrasekaran’s reappointment as chairman for a third five-year term, saying the provision in the company’s Articles of Association requiring a Selection Committee applies to appointing a new Chairman, not to extending or reappointing an incumbent.

While former Supreme Court judges Justice BN Srikrishna and Justice Uday U Lalit opined that the casting vote exercised by the chairman of the Tata Group board was valid under the company’s Articles of Association, the September 17 board resolution giving Chandrasekaran a third term was on lines of a similar one that gave him a second term in 2022, according to legal opinions reviewed in the matter.
Lemon Tree Premier hotel planned in Mumbai

Lemon Tree Hotels Limited today announced that its material subsidiary, Fleur Hotels Limited, has acquired a strategically located land parcel in Bandra (East) adjoining Bandra Kurla Complex, Mumbai to develop a hotel under the “Lemon Tree Premier” brand. The proposed hotel will comprise approximately 172 keys and is planned as an upscale, full-service property catering to growing demand from business travellers, MICE, and the leisure and social segments in the city.

Dr Lal PathLabs to acquire 70% in SN Genelab

The board of Dr Lal PathLabs has approved a 70 per cent stake acquisition in Gujarat-based SN Genelab for about Rs 168 crore. The transaction also includes a performance-linked earn-out capped at Rs 31.5 crore, the company said in a regulatory filing. Following the acquisition, SN Genelab will become a subsidiary of Dr Lal PathLabs.
IDFC First Bank completes CBDT payment integration

IDFC First Bank has completed integration of its payment gateway for CBDT, enabling taxpayers across India to pay direct taxes through multiple digital and physical channels. Taxpayers can choose from multiple payment options, the private sector lender said. The integration with the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) is designed to make tax payments simpler and more convenient for taxpayers, irrespective of their banking relationship, it added.
Balrampur Chini gets Rs 75 crore PLA research grant
Balrampur Chini Mills Ltd has received a Rs 75 crore grant from the Centre to set up a pilot research facility for bio-plastic polylactic acid (PLA) and co-polymer products in Uttar Pradesh.

The company will set up the research and development (R&D) plant at Kumbhi, Uttar Pradesh, with a total capacity of 100 tonnes per annum. The facility will be established at a total cost of Rs 110 crore. Balrampur Chini said the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), under the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India, has provided the Rs 75 crore grant. The company will establish a 100 tonnes per annum PLA Co-Polymer R&D facility under the Government’s flagship BioE3 (Biotechnology for Economy, Environment & Employment) initiative.
PB Fintech flags impact of proposed insurance commission caps

PB Fintech expects India’s proposed caps on insurance commissions to severely affect its non-life insurance business, which may lead to spending cuts and a slowdown in hiring, ‌co-founder and group CEO Yashish Dahiya told analysts on Thursday. The proposals, set out in a consultation paper ‌released on Wednesday, would reintroduce commission caps across life, health and ‌motor insurance that the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India scrapped in 2023.
Laser Power & Infra gets land approval in Kharagpur

Laser Power & Infra Limited announced that it has received a provisional Letter of Intent (LOI) and in-principle approval from the West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation Limited (WBIDC), Government of West Bengal for allotment of approximately 40 acres of industrial land situated at the Vidyasagar Industrial Park in Kharagpur, West Bengal. Laser Power & Infra Limited plans to utilise the newly allotted land to establish a manufacturing facility focused on producing integrated power cables and conductors.
JSW Cement faces proposed Rs 229.85 crore GST demand

JSW Cement Ltd, part of Sajjan Jindal-promoted diversified JSW Group, has received a show-cause notice from the Additional Commissioner of Central Tax, Belagavi Audit Commissionerate, proposing a ₹229.85 crore GST demand, along with applicable interest and a 10% penalty.
Sanofi Healthcare India buys 15.2% stake in Sanofi India

Sanofi Healthcare India, one of the promoter group entities of Sanofi India, on Thursday bought nearly a 15.2 per cent stake in the pharmaceutical company for Rs 1,068 crore through an open market transaction from another promoter, Hoechst GmbH, at an average price of Rs 3,052.
Kinetic Engineering to invest additional Rs 57 crore

Kinetic Group’s flagship firm, Kinetic Engineering Ltd, on Thursday said it will invest an additional Rs 57 crore to expand further and grow the business. The investment comes from the last tranche of conversion of 44,51,000 warrants issued to promoters in March 2025, the company said. Of the total investment, around Rs 17 crore will be directed towards capital expenditure, while Rs 40 crore will be invested in expansion of the company’s electric two-wheeler segment, reflecting KEL’s continued commitment to its electric mobility ambitions, it said.
KPIL secures new orders worth Rs 2,025 crore

Kalpataru Projects International Limited (KPIL) has secured new orders worth around Rs 2,025 crore in the domestic and international markets. The company’s Power Transmission & Distribution (T&D), Buildings and Factories (B&F), and Oil & Gas businesses secured the projects, KPIL said in an exchange filing.
Inox Green Energy launches Rs 600 crore QIP

Inox Green Energy has launched a qualified institutional placement issue at a floor price of Rs 174.36 per equity share. On July 22, the company’s board had approved raising up to Rs 600 crore through multiple financial instruments, including a QIP issue. The company said it may, at its discretion, offer a discount of up to 5 per cent on the floor price calculated for the issue.
Wheels India launches Rs 250 crore QIP

Wheels India has launched a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP) for Rs 250 crore, setting a floor price of Rs 2,197.10 a share. The company has said the indicative issue price for the QIP was fixed at Rs 2,088 a share, a discount of around 4.3% to the company’s Thursday closing price. The issue is expected to dilute approximately 4.7% of Wheels India’s pre-issue equity capital.
ICICI Securities acts as bookrunning manager

ICICI Securities is acting as the bookrunning manager for the issue. The floor price has been determined in accordance with the pricing formula prescribed under the Securities and Exchange Board of India’s ICDR Regulations. The final issue price will be determined in consultation with the bookrunning lead manager.
